clue.text: Thus rich, sly Dad organised much travel for this offspring?

indicators.note: organised means put in order, so the letters of these words are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A family whose wealthy, crafty father has planned a great deal of travel for one of the children.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' rearranges THUS RICH SLY DAD. The nursery rhyme says 'Thursday's child has far to go', hence a child bound for much travel.
explanation.definitionFit: In the rhyme 'Monday's child', the child born on that weekday has far to go, so much travel awaits it.

clue.text: See 4
Game up with outlaw in town

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word for game is read from bottom to top

parts.note: RU is short for rugby union, a game
to outlaw something is to ban it

explanation.surface: A sporting contest moves to the city along with a fugitive outlaw.
explanation.definitionFit: Something urban belongs to the city, so it is to be found in town rather than country.

clue.text: Old devil with letters providing the formula to produce a pet

parts.words: the formula to produce a pet
parts.note: read the other way, screw (twist, distort) the word tape and you produce A PET

explanation.surface: An instruction for making a pet appears to come from a devilish old correspondent.
explanation.walkthrough: C.S. Lewis's The Screwtape Letters are written by a senior devil; 'screw' is taken as an anagram instruction applied to TAPE, giving A PET.
explanation.definitionFit: Screwtape is the senior devil who writes the letters in C.S. Lewis's epistolary novel.

clue.text: Let churlish poet snarl "Time is terrible" with these words?

definitions.text: Let churlish poet snarl "Time is terrible" with these words?

indicators.note: terrible signals that the preceding words are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: A bad-tempered poet growls that time is dreadful, perhaps using a famous line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges LET CHURLISH POET SNARL TIME (24 letters) into the opening line of T.S. Eliot's The Waste Land, and the whole clue describes a gloomy poet saying so.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening line of Eliot's poem complains that a spring month is the harshest, a poet grumbling about time.

clue.text: Name of poet showing sign of sorrow for one in transgressions

indicators.note: for means one thing stands in place of another, so the tear replaces the letter for one

parts.note: transgressions are sins
I is the Roman numeral for one
a tear is a sign of sorrow

explanation.surface: A poet's name crops up where weeping is shown for wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: Stearns is the middle name of Thomas Stearns Eliot, the poet behind the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: T.S. Eliot's middle name was Stearns, so it is a name belonging to the poet.

clue.text: Rodent beginning to tuck into bird no more

indicators.note: into places the initial letter inside the extinct bird's name

parts.note: the huia was a New Zealand bird, now extinct

indicators.note: beginning to picks just the first letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A rodent starts to tuck into a bird that is no longer around.
explanation.definitionFit: The hutia is a Caribbean rodent, a burrowing animal related to guinea pigs.

clue.text: Places of danger to sailors suffering with sore heels

indicators.note: suffering suggests the letters are in a bad way, scrambled into a new order

explanation.surface: Sailors trudge along with painful heels.
explanation.definitionFit: A lee shore is a coast downwind of a ship, perilous because the wind drives vessels onto it.

clue.text: One in society, leader being deposed, may be all but burnt out

definitions.text: may be all but burnt out

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word is removed, as a leader is ousted

parts.note: a member is one belonging to a society

explanation.surface: A society's leader is ousted and the remaining member is exhausted.
explanation.definitionFit: An ember is a smouldering remnant of a fire, nearly but not wholly extinguished.

clue.text: Radiation unit provides information after Head of Oncology participates in opening

indicators.note: after places the word for information at the end
participates in puts the letter inside the word for opening

parts.note: a rent is an opening or tear

indicators.note: Head of takes the first letter of the following word

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A cancer specialist shares information while taking part in an opening ceremony on radiation.
explanation.definitionFit: The roentgen is an old unit measuring exposure to X-ray and gamma radiation.

clue.text: Conjure up Palestine rid of Arafat?

indicators.note: to conjure up is to produce by magic, so the letters are transformed into something new

explanation.surface: A call to make Palestine free of its leader Arafat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conjure up' rearranges PALESTINE RID; Yasser Arafat was President of the Palestinian Authority.
explanation.definitionFit: Arafat held the office of President of the Palestinian Authority, so things of his are of that office.

clue.text: Modernisation may be what library users want

definitions.meaning: bringing something up to date is a renovation or fresh start
borrowers ask to extend the loan period on their books

explanation.surface: Library members would like the building brought up to date.
explanation.definitionFit: Renewal means renovation, and a library loan is extended by renewing it.

clue.text: Someone in pulpit not quiet — one stretching forward?

indicators.note: not says the letter for quiet is removed from the word

parts.note: a preacher speaks from a pulpit
p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: A clergyman in the pulpit is noisy and leans forward.
explanation.definitionFit: A reacher is literally someone who reaches, stretching out an arm or body forward.

clue.text: Most of the time needing a fluid medication

indicators.note: most of says the word loses its final letter

parts.note: time is traditionally the enemy, as in the old question 'how goes the enemy?' meaning what time is it

explanation.surface: Most of the time a patient needs liquid medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'How goes the enemy?' is an old jocular way to ask the time, so time is 'the enemy'.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is a liquid injected into the rectum as a treatment, a fluid medication.

clue.text: Artist with hair up — an American Queen almost

indicators.note: in a down clue, up turns the word for hair upwards

parts.note: a mane is a head of long hair

indicators.note: almost removes the final letter

parts.note: Ellery Queen is the American detective and pen name

explanation.surface: An artist with hair piled up resembles an American queen, almost.
explanation.walkthrough: 'an' is a link word. Ellery Queen was the pen name and hero of American mystery writers.
explanation.definitionFit: An enameller is a craftsman who decorates objects with enamel, a kind of artist.

clue.text: Drunkard stifling call for help — first to rescue is the poet's clairvoyante

indicators.note: stifling means smothering, so the word for drunkard surrounds the distress call

parts.note: a sot is a habitual drunkard
SOS is the distress signal

indicators.note: first to picks the initial letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A drunk stifles a cry for help, and a fortune-teller is the first to come to the rescue.
explanation.walkthrough: Madame Sosostris is the clairvoyante in Eliot's The Waste Land.
explanation.definitionFit: Madame Sosostris is the famous clairvoyante with a wicked pack of cards in Eliot's poem.

clue.text: Clerical doctor has a bit of a scheme concerned with aspect of language

annotationWithheld.why: Clerical doctor has a bit of a scheme concerned with aspect of language (9): 'Clerical doctor' looks like Dr Syntax, but no parse accounts for SYNTAX's X or builds SYNTACTIC from the remaining words
annotationWithheld.clue: Clerical doctor has a bit of a scheme concerned with aspect of language

clue.text: One like Thatcher seen as Queen among dull English?

indicators.note: among places the royal abbreviation inside the word for dull

parts.note: leaden means dull and heavy
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: A woman like Thatcher regarded as queen among dreary Englishmen.
explanation.walkthrough: Leaderene was a mocking nickname for Margaret Thatcher, British prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Leaderene is a jocular term for a domineering female leader, coined for Margaret Thatcher.

clue.text: Blow the whistle when mate is imminently expected?

definitions.meaning: a referee blows to finish a match
in chess, the final phase when checkmate is near

explanation.surface: A referee signals that a romantic partner is about to arrive.
explanation.definitionFit: A referee's whistle may close a match, and the final phase of chess when checkmate looms has that name.

clue.text: Euphemism for rude word that's death to one esteemed sir

parts.note: eff stands in for a well-known swear word
death is the end
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A polite substitute for a swear word proves fatal to a respected gentleman.
explanation.walkthrough: Effendi is a Turkish title of respect for an educated man.
explanation.definitionFit: Effendi is an honorific used in Turkey and the Middle East for a man of standing.

clue.text: Taking a spin around the Home Counties, the Spanish gentleman moved slowly

indicators.note: around puts the turned title on either side of the region's letters
taking a spin means turning round, so the gentleman's title is read backwards

parts.note: Don is a Spanish gentleman's title
SE, south-east, covers the Home Counties, the counties around London

explanation.surface: A Spanish gentleman drove slowly on a spin through the counties around London.
explanation.definitionFit: To nose is to move forward slowly and carefully, as a car noses out of a junction.

clue.text: Second eleven chap moved fast

parts.note: an eleven is a team, as in cricket or football
Ed is a man's name, any chap

explanation.surface: A man from the reserve team ran off quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamed is informal for went at speed, as a train under full steam.

clue.text: See 4
Bulldoze the accommodation between numbers 9 and 11?

parts.note: a flat is a place to live
ten falls between nine and eleven

explanation.surface: A developer threatens to demolish the property sitting between houses numbered nine and eleven.
explanation.definitionFit: To bulldoze a building is to flatten it, leveling it to the ground.

clue.text: Revolutionary soldiers in foremost company

indicators.note: in places the turned soldiers inside the word for foremost

parts.note: top means foremost, leading

indicators.note: revolutionary means turning round, so the letters for soldiers are reversed

parts.note: OR, other ranks, means ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: Rebel troops are in the leading unit.
explanation.definitionFit: A troop is a company or band, especially a group of soldiers or performers.

clue.text: Green growth very good? The last thing you want on lawn!

definitions.text: Green growth very good? The last thing you want on lawn!

parts.note: a plant is green growth
A1, written AI, means first-class

indicators.text: The last thing you want on
indicators.note: the last thing picks the final letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders whether a green plant is good, but certainly not on the lawn.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a lawn weed while building it: PLANT, AI (A1) and the final letter of 'lawn'.
explanation.definitionFit: Plantain is a broad-leaved weed, green growth that gardeners hate seeing on their lawns.

clue.text: Beginning of the Hindu festival in round buildings

indicators.note: beginning of selects the first letter of the next word

parts.note: Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours

explanation.surface: The start of a Hindu festival is held in domed buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tholi is the plural of tholus, a circular domed building or tomb.

clue.text: Is pi chap out with oracle from Canterbury?

indicators.note: out signals the words are put out of order, rearranged

explanation.surface: A man of religion consults an oracle in Canterbury.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges IS PI CHAP ORACLE; Canterbury is the seat of the Archbishop who leads the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Archiepiscopal means belonging to an archbishop, as the see of Canterbury is.
